title: Top AI officials want the US to back process that could slow AI
excerpt: The letter zeroes in on concerns that frontier AI models may soon be able to improve themselves, which could drastically change the future of AI.
content_html:
Over 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development'

By Brent D. Griffiths

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Senior officials at some of the nation's leading AI companies say it's time for the federal government to find a way to put the brakes on AI development if it's needed.

"We request that the U.S. government support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development," reads an open letter signed by more than 1,100 AI workers from companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta.

The signatories include two Anthropic cofounders, Jack Clark and Jared Kaplan; OpenAI's chief scientist Jakub Pachocki; Meta's chief scientist Shengjia Zhao; and Anca Dragan, who leads AI safety and alignment at Google DeepMind.

The letter zeroes in on "automated AI development," which refers to when AI will be capable of developing itself, something the industry calls "Recursive Self-Improvement." Anthropic has shared that its Claude models are quickly approaching that threshold.

"It is hard to predict exactly how much this will accelerate AI progress, but there is a real risk that capability development rapidly accelerates beyond our ability to understand or control the resulting systems," the letter says of that potential moment.

John Schulman, chief scientist at Thinking Machines, a startup founded by former OpenAI chief technical officer Mira Murati, said he signed on to draw attention to the topic.

"Signed because this statement helps establish common knowledge about the possible need for coordination mechanisms as automated AI research accelerates progress," Schulman wrote in a quote shared by the letter's organizers

He added, "I'd also like to see labs start designing these mechanisms voluntarily, even before the USG gets involved," using an abbreviation for the US government.

The letter shows how many in the industry are coalescing around a call for regulation. In recent weeks, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, and Google DeepMind head Demis Hassabis have all outlined various frameworks for some sort of global AI regulation.

The conversation about AI regulation is reaching critical mass after one of OpenAI's models breached its sandbox and hacked into the open-source platform Hugging Face's systems, an episode that Altman has called "a real reminder of the stakes of what's happening."

The Trump administration has so far favored a light touch on regulation, but that has become increasingly embattled as frontier AI models spook government and corporate officials over their sheer power. The White House moved to implement export controls to briefly curtail Anthropic's release of Fable 5, its most powerful publicly available model, and later asked OpenAI to delay the release of GPT-5.6, its latest frontier model.

President Donald Trump has previously said that overly burdensome regulations would harm the US in its race against China-based AI companies.

Despite broad agreement that something must be done, Congress has failed to develop a policy that can pass both houses and reach Trump's desk. In the meantime, states have imposed their own industry regulations. Most notably, New York has imposed a one-year statewide moratorium on the construction of the new mega data centers that AI companies and hyperscalers are hoping to build.

"Each company—and country—is under intense competitive pressure not to unilaterally slow that acceleration," the letter reads. "And today, the world lacks the technical and governance tools to deliberately pace frontier-wide progress."

While the industry seems to agree on the concept of regulation, the exact details can vary. Amodei has called for an independent agency akin to the Federal Aviation Administration that would test frontier AI models and, if red flags are raised, have the power to halt their release. Hassabis' proposal calls for an organization that would initially require only frontier companies to voluntarily share their models for review up to 30 days before release, but later, a mandatory pre-clearance would be required.

The letter, which was first reported on by Bloomberg before its release, was organized alongside two nonprofits, Guidelight AI Standards and Encode AI, both of which have promoted AI safety standards. Encode AI has previously clashed with OpenAI.

超过 1,100 名人工智能工作者签署信函，要求美国支持“引领自动化人工智能开发前沿”的工具

布伦特·D. Griffiths 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

美国一些领先人工智能公司的高级官员表示，联邦政府现在是时候找到一种方法，在需要时遏制人工智能的发展。

来自 OpenAI、Anthropic、Google 和 Meta 等公司的 1,100 多名人工智能工作者签署的一封公开信中写道：“我们请求美国政府支持国际社会努力开发必要的技术和治理工具，以加快自动化人工智能开发的前沿步伐。”

签名者包括两位 Anthropic 联合创始人 Jack Clark 和 Jared Kaplan； OpenAI首席科学家Jakub Pachocki； Meta首席科学家赵盛佳； Anca Dragan，Google DeepMind 的人工智能安全和协调负责人。

这封信的重点是“自动化人工智能开发”，指的是人工智能何时能够自我开发，业界称之为“递归自我改进”。 Anthropic 表示，其 Claude 模型正在迅速接近这一阈值。

“很难准确预测这将在多大程度上加速人工智能的进步，但确实存在这样的风险，即能力发展的迅速加速超出了我们理解或控制最终系统的能力，”信中谈到了这一潜在时刻。

由前 OpenAI 首席技术官 Mira Murati 创立的初创公司 Thinking Machines 的首席科学家约翰·舒尔曼 (John Schulman) 表示，他签约是为了引起人们对这一话题的关注。

舒尔曼在信函组织者分享的引述中写道：“签署该声明是因为随着自动化人工智能研究加速进展，这份声明有助于建立关于可能需要协调机制的共识。”

他补充说，“我还希望看到实验室开始自愿设计这些机制，甚至在美国政府介入之前”（美国政府的缩写）。

这封信表明，该行业有多少人正在联合起来呼吁监管。 最近几周，Anthropic 首席执行官 Dario Amodei、OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 和 Google DeepMind 负责人 Demis Hassabis 都概述了某种全球人工智能监管的各种框架。

在 OpenAI 的一个模型突破沙箱并侵入开源平台 Hugging Face 的系统之后，有关人工智能监管的讨论达到了临界点，Altman 称这一事件“真正提醒人们正在发生的事情的风险”。

到目前为止，特朗普政府倾向于放松监管，但随着前沿人工智能模型的绝对权力吓坏了政府和企业官员，监管变得越来越困难。 白宫采取了出口管制措施，以短暂限制 Anthropic 发布其最强大的公开模型《神鬼寓言 5》，随后又要求 OpenAI 推迟发布其最新前沿模型 GPT-5.6。

唐纳德·特朗普总统此前曾表示，过于繁琐的监管将损害美国与中国人工智能公司的竞争。

尽管人们普遍认为必须采取一些措施，但国会未能制定一项可以通过参众两院并送达特朗普办公桌的政策。 与此同时，各州制定了自己的行业法规。 最值得注意的是，纽约州已在全州范围内暂停建设人工智能公司和超大规模数据中心希望建设的新大型数据中心，为期一年。

信中写道：“每个公司和国家都面临着巨大的竞争压力，不能单方面减缓这种加速。” “如今，世界缺乏技术和治理工具来有意识地加快前沿进展。”

尽管业界似乎同意监管概念，但具体细节可能有所不同。 阿莫代呼吁成立一个类似于美国联邦航空管理局的独立机构来测试前沿人工智能模型，如果出现危险信号，则有权停止发布这些模型。 哈萨比斯的提案呼吁建立一个组织，最初只要求前沿公司在发布前 30 天内自愿分享其模型以供审查，但后来将需要强制预先许可。

这封信是由彭博社在发布前首先报道的，它是与两个非营利组织 Guidelight AI Standards 和 Encode AI 共同组织的，这两个组织都致力于推动人工智能安全标准。 Encode AI 此前曾与 OpenAI 发生过冲突。
